_derivation.measured: 2026-10-21, Apple M-series laptop, 10 cores, Bun 1.4.3, `bun run bench:gate` (profile ci), machine shared with other jobs (load average 12-13). Local values are in the _local keys.
_derivation.throughput floors: local x 0.6 (one GitHub ubuntu-latest vCPU is roughly 0.6x one laptop core) x 0.6 (margin for runner noise) = about 0.36 x local, rounded down.
_derivation.latency/size ceilings: local / 0.36, rounded up, then generous: they catch order-of-magnitude regressions (a sync call on the hot path, a leak), not 10% drifts.
_derivation.load: The CI load profile publishes at a fixed 400 ev/s (1,000 readers, 15 s), well under the server's capacity even on 2 vCPUs, so accepted_eps must keep up with the schedule (95%), nothing may be lost (delivered/expected, errors), and the latencies/lag show queueing.
_derivation.local overrides: BENCH_<BENCH>_<METRIC>_<MIN|MAX>=n for one bound, BENCH_SCALE=f to multiply every min (and divide every max) by f, BENCH_THRESHOLDS=<file> for another file.
_derivation.after write-path work: 2026-10-21, same laptop, load average 4-6: load 3.6 ms OK p95, 1.0 ms lag p99, 219 MB RSS; verify inline 3,790 / pool 6,519 ev/s; storage ingest 6,105 ev/s, author feed 0.79 ms; fanout 74,208 / 3,706 ev/s. Bounds kept: most of the gain is the quieter machine (ingest alone varies 4.1k-6.1k here) and the load profile is a fixed 400 ev/s.

load._local: accepted 500/500 ev/s target run, ok p95 7.8 ms, delivery p95 8.0 ms, ratio 1.0, 0 errors, RSS peak 133 MB, loop lag p99 6.3 ms

verify._local: inline 2,486 ev/s, pool (2 threads) 2,611 ev/s; on a 2-vCPU runner the default pool is 1 thread

storage._local: ingest 4,133 ev/s (30k events), author feed query 1.46 ms

fanout._local: broadcast 56,004 ev/s through 10k subscriptions, engine ingest 2,873 ev/s
